note.title: Case-role introduction
note.overview: Five preserved source-backed case-role recognition questions, plus fifteen supplementary application, independent-recall and translation questions aligned with the same taught grammar rules.
learningGoals: Identify the grammatical clue and apply it accurately.
Identify grammatical roles despite varying Latin word order.
Independently translate case-based sentences and justify subject/object roles.
mustMemoriseRules: Common English meaning: in / on, with, by, from.

What is the main role of the genitive case?

workedExamples.answer: Location / method / instrument; often with prepositions
workedExamples.why: Common English meaning: in / on, with, by, from.

commonMistakes: Choosing a case from word order instead of grammatical function.
Recognising one familiar word without checking the complete grammatical clue.
detailedExplanation: This note supports 5 source-backed questions on Case-role introduction.

Latin noun endings show the word's grammatical job as well as number. Identify the dictionary form and stem, decide the required case and number from the sentence, then select the ending. Translate the function, not simply the first familiar meaning.
examTips: Mark the finite verb first, then use noun endings to assign subject, object and recipient roles.
Normal Latin word order can vary; the case, number, gender, person and tense endings cannot.
For English to Latin, build each required form before arranging the sentence.
